question: A 60-year-old man with extensive ulcerative colitis of 15 years of evolution and in clinical remission in the last 3 years, comes to our consultation to learn about the risk of colorectal cancer and the possibility of participating in prevention programs. It is correct to inform you that:

options.opa: Ulcerative colitis is only associated with an increased risk of colorectal cancer in smokers.
options.opb: In your case, given that you are in long-term remission, the screening recommended to the general population is considered appropriate.
options.opc: In cases like yours, it is considered appropriate to undergo periodic colonoscopies with multiple staggered biopsies taken throughout the entire colon.
options.opd: In cases like yours, screening by periodic occult blood studies in feces but with a frequency higher than that used in the screening of the general population is considered adequate.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Ulcerative colitis -> increased risk of colorectal cancer -> especially after 8-10 years of disease duration -> 80% CHAIN: Clinical remission in ulcerative colitis -> does not eliminate the risk of colorectal cancer -> surveillance still necessary -> 85% CHAIN: Long-term remission in ulcerative colitis -> may reduce but not eliminate the risk of colorectal cancer -> surveillance still recommended -> 80% CHAIN: Periodic colonoscopies with multiple biopsies in entire colon -> recommended for surveillance in ulcerative colitis -> especially in cases of long-standing disease -> 90% CHAIN: Screening by periodic occult blood studies in feces -> may not be sufficient for surveillance in ulcerative colitis -> colonoscopy preferred -> 80%
analysis: In cases of extensive ulcerative colitis with long-term remission, the risk of colorectal cancer is increased. Therefore, more intensive screening measures are usually recommended to detect any potential malignancy at an early stage.
